beats.say: True or false? This tiny shrimp shoots a bubble almost as hot as the sun.
beats.quiz:
THIS SHRIMP'S
BUBBLE IS AS HOT
AS THE SUN
beats.bonus: The snap of a pistol shrimp is one of the loudest sounds in the ocean, louder than a gunshot up close.
beats.short_title: Is a Pistol Shrimp's Bubble as Hot as the Sun? 🦐

beats.say: True! Well, almost. When a pistol shrimp snaps its claw, it fires a bubble that collapses at around four thousand seven hundred degrees Celsius. The surface of the sun is about five thousand five hundred.
The snap is so powerful it stuns small fish, and the whole thing lasts less than a blink. This shrimp hunts with a sonic boom.
It doesn't need a gun. It is the gun.
True or false? If a bear chases you, run downhill.
beats.bonus: Bear spray is one of the most effective ways to stop a charging bear, according to US park rangers.
beats.short_title: Should You Run Downhill From a Bear? 🐻

beats.say: False! Bears run downhill just fine, at up to about thirty five miles an hour. You can't outrun a bear in any direction.
Park rangers say don't run at all. Running can make a bear chase you. Stay calm, talk, back away slowly, and carry bear spray.
Downhill just means it catches you faster.
True or false? Sharks are older than trees.
beats.bonus: Sharks survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs about sixty six million years ago.
beats.short_title: Are Sharks Really Older Than Trees? 🦈

beats.say: True! Sharks have been swimming around for roughly four hundred and fifty million years. The first trees showed up around three hundred and eighty five million years ago.
That means sharks were already ancient when the first forest grew. They also outlived the dinosaurs.
Sharks are basically the grandparents of the planet.
True or false? A turtle can crawl out of its shell.
beats.quiz:
A TURTLE CAN
CRAWL OUT OF
ITS SHELL
beats.bonus: A turtle's shell is covered in scutes, made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails.
beats.short_title: Can a Turtle Come Out of Its Shell? 🐢

beats.say: False! A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton. Its ribs and backbone are fused right into it.
So a turtle without its shell isn't a naked turtle. It's a turtle without a skeleton. Cartoons lied to you again.
The shell isn't a house. It's the turtle.
True or false? One tick bite can make you allergic to steak.
beats.quiz:
ONE TICK BITE
CAN MAKE YOU
ALLERGIC TO STEAK
beats.bonus: The lone star tick is named for the white spot on the female's back.
beats.short_title: Can a Tick Bite Make You Allergic to Red Meat? 🥩

beats.say: True! A bite from the lone star tick can trigger alpha-gal syndrome, an allergy to red meat like beef and pork.
The reaction often shows up hours after eating, which makes it hard to figure out. Doctors in the United States have been seeing more and more cases.
One tiny bite, and burgers are cancelled.
True or false? Baby koalas eat their mom's poop.
beats.quiz:
BABY KOALAS
EAT THEIR
MOM'S POOP
beats.bonus: Eucalyptus leaves are so low in energy that koalas sleep up to around twenty hours a day.
beats.short_title: Do Baby Koalas Really Eat Poop? 🐨

beats.say: True! Before a joey can eat eucalyptus leaves, its mom makes a special soft poop called pap, and the joey eats it.
Pap is packed with the gut microbes the baby needs to digest eucalyptus, which is tough and toxic to most animals.
Baby's first meal. Delicious.
True or false? Cows kill more Americans than sharks do.
beats.quiz:
COWS KILL MORE
AMERICANS
THAN SHARKS
beats.bonus: Many cow-related deaths involve protective mothers or bulls on farms.
beats.short_title: Do Cows Really Kill More People Than Sharks? 🐄

beats.say: True! In the United States, cattle are linked to about twenty deaths a year. Sharks average about one.
Most of those cow accidents happen on farms, from kicks and charges. Sharks just have a much scarier publicist.
Jaws should have been about a cow.
True or false? Polar bears aren't white.
beats.bonus: A polar bear's black skin helps soak up warmth from the sun.

beats.say: True! A polar bear's skin is black, and its hairs are actually clear. They scatter light, so the coat looks white.
The black skin helps soak up the sun's warmth, and the thick coat holds it in. A polar bear dresses for the Arctic.
A black bear in a white coat.
True or false? Shave a tiger, and it's still striped.
beats.quiz:
SHAVE A TIGER,
IT'S STILL
STRIPED
beats.bonus: No two tigers have the same stripe pattern.
beats.short_title: Is a Tiger's Skin Striped Too? 🐯

beats.say: True! A tiger's stripes aren't just on its fur. The skin underneath is striped too.
And every tiger's pattern is different, like a fingerprint. Please do not test this one yourself.
Stripes all the way down.
True or false? A cockroach can live for a week without its head.
beats.quiz:
A COCKROACH CAN
LIVE A WEEK
WITHOUT ITS HEAD
beats.bonus: Cockroaches can hold their breath for around forty minutes.
beats.short_title: Can a Cockroach Really Live Without Its Head? 🪳

beats.say: True! Cockroaches breathe through tiny holes along their body, not through their head. So losing it doesn't stop them breathing.
Without a mouth, it can't drink, so it eventually dies of thirst, after about a week.
Headless, and somehow still fine.
